assessment: This manuscript investigates the role of the repressor-element 1-silencing transcription/neuron-restrictive silencer factor (REST/NRSF) in homeostatic regulation of neuronal activity in response to chronic hyperactivity in cultured neural networks. This work demonstrates the role of REST in network firing properties and specifically the role of inhibition in this regulation. This paper is of potential interest to a broad audience of neuroscientists, interested in the mechanisms of homeostatic plasticity and in brain disorders associated with neural dyshomeostasis.
